sources.evidence: LOU-100 bench (Grok's Bot 2): gpt-5.4-mini 0/3 with corrupt patches; gpt-6.2-sol passed but took shortcuts. gpt-6.2-sol billed payer=developer 2026-11-18 15:39 PST and 2026-11-19 07:00 and 10:19 PST.
sources.request_ids: The Free Pool project only allows base aliases (a dated id returned 403 model_not_found on 2026-11-19), so requests use the alias and the served snapshot must equal listed_id.

fleet.note: No shared filesystem across machines, so each machine may use only its share of each group's fleet ceiling. The shares sum to 1.0, so the fleet cannot jointly cross a ceiling.

official_1M.note: Launch/Grow 1M token group, shared across every model in it. A request that would cross the cap is billed in full. The pool is org-wide: traffic outside these ledgers (other lanes, Agents sessions, OpenCode) also uses it, so a payer!=openai row blocks the group for the rest of the UTC day.

official_10M.note: Launch/Grow 10M token group, shared across every model in it. A request that would cross the cap is billed in full.

empirical_6.2.note: Not on the help article's lists. Evidence on 2026-11-19 shows these calls share the org's 1M daily pool: after the M5 probes, gpt-5.5 was free at 65 tokens and billed at 136, then gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.2-astra were billed at 65 tokens each on the Mac Pro. That matches the help article's 'a request that would cross the cap is billed in full' rule, with the pool nearly full and smaller requests still fitting. So usage counts toward official_1M, and a billed row in either group blocks both for the UTC day. Sol is off; Astra needs --hard.

default_request_caps.note: Applied to any model without its own caps. Raise a cap only with payer=openai evidence at that size.

hard_blocks.reason: -pro and gpt-5.3-codex were billed (gpt-5.5-pro probe returned payer=developer); gpt-4.5-preview is shut down.
